pr_title: drivers: CAN: Abstract blocking send call
pr_body:
This commit moves the semaphore for a blocking call from
the driver implementation to the stack of the caller.
It reduces the complexity of the drivers and saves some RAM.

Fixes #22379

issue_context.title: stm32: can_send gets stuck (ignoring timeout) if bus not present
issue_context.body:
If the transceiver is not wired to the bus, `can_stm32_send` gets stuck after 3 calls (= length of the internal TX queue of the used STM32F072) in the following line:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ac12066800ac0d7c2e353462b830f96e8e97fe1b/drivers/can/can_stm32.c#L630

Changing the  `k_sem_take` timeout from `K_FOREVER` to `timeout` (= function argument) solved the problem. But I'm not sure if this is the ideal solution, @alexanderwachter .

I'm currently using the CAN interface in a very simple way without any callbacks:
`can_send(can_dev, &msg, K_MSEC(10), NULL, NULL);`
comments:
We are already aware of this situation.
Tho problem is that the frame is in the mailbox already and we cant remove it from there.
#20890 is the fix for it.
Great, thanks. And sorry that I didn't look carefully enough in the open PRs.

> Great, thanks. And sorry that I didn't look carefully enough in the open PRs.

No problem. I always try to label all CAN related PRs and Issues with "area: CAN"

@martinjaeger I would say this is the expected behaviour. The timeout in `can_send()` is for acquiring a TX MB, not a transmission timeout (as such a transmission timeout would be rather difficult to honour on many CAN controllers, which tend to always retransmit in hardware). By default, the CAN controller will attempt to retransmit frames without ACK or when arbitration is lost, which would happen if no CAN transceiver/CAN bus is connected.

With the recent changes to the API documentation in #41845, hopefully this behaviour is more clear. The same PR also introduced "one-shot" mode for the STM32 CAN controller, which will disable the automatic retransmission in hardware and perhaps be closer to the behaviour, you expect?

I agree that it can be considered expected behaviour, so we can probably close the issue.

As far as I can see, the one-shot mode can only be configured via Devicetree. If that's the case, it is not useful for my application, as I want to use the same CAN interface either in "fire & forget" mode for low priority messages or with proper error checking for ISO-TP. But it's not a big deal, I created an empty callback so that `can_send` still returns if the mailbox is full because of transmission errors.

review_comments:
This change will introduce an overhead of initialising a semaphore on each `can_send()` call without any callback defined. I am not sure it is worth it.

It also seem very unlike any other API implementation in Zephyr?

Yea I am sort of ambivalent about it. Not sure how much of a trade-off the memory saved vs the calling overhead it is. 
In terms of driver complexity I think it isn't a big improvement, we all had the same approach and it's not so hard to follow either.

>This change will introduce an overhead of initialising a semaphore on each can_send() call without any callback defined. I am not sure it is worth it.

The overhead of initializing is not that much. The blocking send call is used rarely, and in the current implementation, we need to maintain a sem for every mailbox just in case we will need it.

>In terms of driver complexity I think it isn't a big improvement, we all had the same approach and it's not so hard to follow either.

The complexity raised with the timeout patch :-)
I really don't like #19707 in its current state.
Ah gotcha. What would be your plan then, use that can_common_isr_callback_handler() for failing sends with timeouts?
Updated #19707 on top of this PR. Looks better now!
